reports.title: Molly Russell: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: There was no separation between adult and child parts of the platforms or separate platforms for children and adults
concerns.hazard: lack of platform separation for children

concerns.quote: There was no age verification when signing up to the on-line platform
That the content was not controlled so as to be age specific
That algorithms were used to provide content together with adverts
That the parent, guardian or carer did not have access, to the material being viewed or any control over that material
That the child's account was not capable of being separately linked to the parent, guardian or carer's account for monitoring

reports.title: Isabella Shere: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: There are questions and answers on Quora's website that provide information [REDACTED]. The question and answer thread that Miss Shere viewed immediately before her death, at the time of writing this report has had 169,700 views.

Children are able to access the site through search engines without being required to create an account and access content [REDACTED] without being asked if they are an adult or being required to input their date of birth.
There is a function to follow questions [REDACTED] encouraging further consumption of this material.
There is not sufficient monitoring and/or moderation of the content of questions/answers in accordance with Quora's own platform policies. [REDACTED]

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of age verification that allows children to view unsuitable content. The earlier report focuses on sign‑up checks, while the later report notes that children can reach the content via search without any age confirmation.
links.earlier_quote: There was no age verification when signing up to the on-line platform.
